title: Botscape
tagline: A massively multiplayer online game for artificial intelligence players.
description:
Several years ago, the computer science club at the University of Waterloo ran an AI challenge: they created a game and people from around the world wrote programs to play the game, competing for dominance.
We decided to take this idea further. Rather than participating in many short games against a small number of other programs, bots in Botscape are placed into a massive world with every other bot. They play a single, continuous game of epic proportions.
The infinite world and continuous gameplay style offer a new experience in AI programming. Developers will find unique challenges that will help them improve their skills.
Users can upload bots and watch them compete live. If they spot problems, they can upload new versions, which are inserted into the world almost immediately.

title: Flock
tagline: The social door lock
description:
I moved into a new place and didn't want to carry around a ring of keys. My friends and family constantly visit me, and I am not always home to let them in. A Wi-Fi connected, socially aware door lock just made sense.
I am most proud of Flock's ability to automagically let friends in when there is an event scheduled at my house, and they have RSVPd.

title: Guava
tagline: Secure patient genome browsing on the web
description:
Guava= Genomes for User Accessible Variant Annotation
Hospitals around the world are beginning to sequence patient DNA. These data, referred to collectively as patient genomes, are large data sets that require interpretation. Once interpreted, genomic data can inform many medical decisions including disease prediction and predisposition to diseases such as cancer, drug responses using pharmacogenomics and identifying genetic causes of disease.
Many annotation tools exist for genomes, but no open source web applications have emerged for clinical annotation of genomes and presentation of results.
We have developed a comprehensive API to process patient genomic sequence data from standard Variant Call Format (VCF) files and annotate these variants. Our annotation pipeline uses a messaging queue to achieve robust scalability that is ready for a cloud infrastructure.
The Guava API is designed for the clinic. We have implemented the technology to function independently on a local hospital cluster. A key-based authentication system provides secure access for authorized clinical users to only access their patients. The genomic variant queries can be performed rapidly, which is critical for whole genome sequence data which can contain upwards of 5 million variant rows per patient. Variants are annotated with gene effects, allele frequency, clinical significance and human phenotype ontology terms, and this list can be expanded using the open source annovar pipeline.
As a proof of concept we have constructed a web application that provides access to authenticated users to upload and annotate their genomic VCF files. Once uploaded, clinical users can access all annotated patient data.
We intend to beta test this service in the clinic.

title: Lend
tagline: The airbnb for things.
description:
We are Lend. We make it easy for people to both borrow and rent out items within their community. WIth the Airbnb's and Uber's of the world, the economy of sharing is booming, and we look to bring that to the rental and loaning market. Lend looks to address two key problems within this market:
1) We have so many items in our house that we rarely use that were expensive to buy. Why not be able to rent these items from people in the local community, as well as make money renting out items for others to use?
2) Classifieds like Craigslist and Kijiji show offers for rentals, but provide no attempt to help the process of rental. Lend provide's ease of use and transparency during these transactions, including providing smooth communication and payment handling between them.

title: Open Pokémon
tagline: It's not just a game.
description:
Open Pokémon  takes the dreams of every single 90s kid and let's them become Pokémon masters - but in the real world!
Implementing a variety of hardware and APIs, Open Pokémon takes the actions of Pokémon  trainers and allows users to emulate them.
The journey begins with walking around with your phone. A map is generated based on your location through Google. Random encounters with wild Pokemon can be won through using voice commands to get Pokémon to attack (through Wit.ai), and when weakened, Pokéballs can be thrown with a throwing motion (using the Thalmic Myo). To ensure that you've caught them all, simply "Open Pokédex" to view which of the 151 original you have left to catch, and once you're ready to move on, "Hide Pokédex"!
Once your team is stacked, duke it out with your friends with our multi-player options, and battle to be the very best!
Remember to continually check the status of your Pokémon though! Your Pokéwatch (Pebble Watch) will send reminders to go to the nearest Pokémon Center by displaying your party status. And once you're done for the day, head home to your computer and  show some affection for your Pokémon by patting and rubbing them (through the Leap Motion). Make sure to care for all your Pokémon - simply cycle through with a circular motion!
Are you ready to be the next Pokémon Master?

title: pinpnt.me
tagline: Quick and clean location-sharing
description:
pinpnt.me
where the
$#%^!
are you?
pinpnt.me
is a quick and clean location sharing app. Share your location as easily as sharing a link to co-ordinate a meet up, or track your own location as you move around!
Inspiration
Meeting up with people, especially in crowded or unfamiliar places is hard. Assembling at the University of Waterloo for Hack The North was especially difficult since half our team is from out of town, and one of our members arrived much after dark, when it was difficult to identify both building landmarks and street signs.
Here's an outline of what typically happens
without
pinpnt.me
:
Be confused about where you are
Be confused about where your friend is
Send a text to your friend and wait 5 minutes for no reply
Call your friend, who doesn't hear the phone ring because it's too loud
Walk around aimlessly trying to find your friend
Repeat several times
Feel sad
Here's an outline of the typical user's experience
with
pinpnt.me
:
Be confused about where you are in a foreign or crowded position
Open
pinpnt.me
Share link with a friend (or many!)
Friend(s) open the link, share their locations
Walk/otherwise transport yourself with the guidance of your friends
Meet up!
Close
pinpnt.me
Target Audience
The lost and/or confused. Anyone looking for a super-quick way to find people.
Awesome Key Features
pinpnt.me
is a lightweight web app that uses the Google Maps API to help people find themselves and each other (in a literal sense).
No names
No records
No OS exclusivity
No registration required
The overriding design goal for pinpnt.me
was to make it as clean and simple as possible. 
The idea is that finding yourself and your friends
should be as easy as possible, without the hassle of 
signing up for a service, downloading an app, or worrying that your location
data will be recorded or logged.
Tech
pinpnt.me
uses a number of awesome code-things work properly:
Cassandra
- highly scalable database (also used by Facebook!)
Flask Python
- lightweight Python framework
Google Maps API
- because maps.
jQuery JavaScript
- duh.
Installation
No need to install, this is a web app.
License
GPL
About the Hackers
We're a group of first year's from a few different schools, who graduated in the same high school class. We get lost on a fairly regular basis.
Justin Li
: University of Waterloo
Alice Ma
: Queen's University
Ryan Marks
: McMaster University
Eric Ye
: University of Waterloo

title: RememberAlll
tagline: Curating life's most precious experiences into a beautiful and searchable archive
description: Pictures can never truly save the gorgeous spontaneity of life. Most of your most precious experiences happen without you expecting it. In order to capture these moments, we created RememberAll, a Google Glass application that streams video and audio in real time. Our parallelized backend infrastructure analyzes videos frame by frame and transcribes audio to tag each second with rich, structured information within 5 minutes of capture. We then power a web application with fuzzy search to rediscover this content on your computer and compose journal entries and articles in a way that was never before possible.

title: SignLang
tagline: By using a LeapMotion and a Myo armband, we created a sign language translator.
description: This project started out as an ambition as we were on the bus to coming to HackTheNorth. We wanted to take as much hardware and do something sensible with all the technology. Neville decided that we could do something involving sign language as he was making gestures with his hand. And thus SignLang was born. As many as 2 million people rely on sign language to communicate and now they will be able to communicate with the 7 billion people of the world. We are using a LeapMotion and a Myo in order to detect hand and arm movements and then using meSpeak to speak once the letter has been identified.

title: Silicon Man
tagline: Iron Man's hipster tech cousin.
description:
Tired of having to pull out your phone and check your emails? Wish you could record every second of your life? Pockets too small to hold a smartphone?
Never fear, the Silicon Man invention is here to help. By attaching your smartphone on a 100% futuristic helmet-mask-thingy, and then strapping it onto your face - you are always connected to the CLOUD 24/7. Need to check your email? It's right there! Trying to impress your boss? Look up the Wikipedia entry and start impressing!
Ofcourse you won't be using the touchscreen like some chump, we have included the next level advancement in technology - the Swag-Glove. With sensors and buttons attached right to your limb, you can control your new high-tech face mask through gestures and flexes!!!!!
Patent-pending. Batteries sold separately.

title: Spacebowl
tagline: Bowling in space with the Oculus Rift and Myo
description:
Spacebowl
Starting as a snowball fight game, Spacebowl pivoted into something which everyone likes - bowling. Throw on your Oculus and Myo to be immersed in an awesome VR experience. Strike out with Spacebowl!

title: 25$ Arduino Syringe Pump
tagline: 2000% cost savings comes with variable micro litre to milli litre accuracy!
description:
We needed a syringe pump to run our startup Suncayr. We're a group of nanotechnology engineers making a colour changing marker that you can draw on your skin that will let you know when to re-apply sunscreen.
We were left with the gloomy outlook of having to purchase a 500$ syringe pump, when all we want to do is use the money we've been able to raise from winning pitch and product competitions towards valuable research.
We created a 25$ syringe pump that is scalable and accurate. It can pump on the milli litre range or micro litre range. We can further integrate the Arduino with the rest of the equipment in our lab to fully automate our synthesis procedures - this is something that is never done in a traditional research lab, but will greatly improve Suncayr's efficiency in the future.

title: 3D Chai Crystals: Augmented Reality
tagline: Augmented. Hypnotic. 3D.
description:
The Chai Crystal started out as a single, flat, still design. I decided for my hack I wanted to explore the python scripting extension in Cinema 4D R15 while the backend hackers in my group slept, to see if I could animate the crystal. When I created a gif for my business cards I never thought to create a hack with the flat design. But I was inspired by the possibility of 3D animated crystals and their hypnotic and augmented reality feel.
So I started from scratch, re-created the crystals in Cinema 4D, coded some position tracks and brought in some materials. I then reflected and positioned certain elements to create a cool "fill and reflect" effect. I am proud with how they turned out.
My goal with this hack would be to bring the crystals into some type of augmented reality or digitized platform that could project them or allow users to interact with them: Whether the user would move it on their own with Thalmic Myo or Leap Motion technology or have it within their Pebble on their wrist. I am really excited to learn more about augmented reality, 3D and 4D technology.
I spent the last few hours of the hackathon with another hacker from Penn State, Brennan Cornell, working to get a working prototype with Leap Motion, inspired by the Elon Musk & Leap Motion Cad Model.
Unfortunately the API wouldn't update and run correctly in Java so we couldn't get a working demo but it was still fun getting it to the demo stage and working with the technology!
concept demo video:
https://vimeo.com/106715525
password: 36hours

title: A day in ...
tagline: Get all your sightseeing done in one day - optimized routing for tourists.
description:
There’s a fine line between technically interesting and useful, and technically boring.
We wanted to build something that would be a real world application of the CS theory we learn in the classroom - specifically, optimization, routing, NP problems - but which would also be valuable to the general public.
Rather than reinvent the wheel, we took two APIs - a routing API by Routific and Yelp’s Place API - and create a web application that would enable a tourist/visitor to maximize his time in a city by providing an optimized route through the top attractions in a given city.
Neither of us are front-end developers so we wanted to push the envelope by shifting the focus of this app to use Angular.js. A hackathon seemed like a great time to learn how to hack in an unfamiliar language! We’re most proud of the way we’ve combined two APIs in a novel way  - heck, make that three (we used Google Maps for geocoding too!) - to create something that people are actually going to use and which hackers can respect.
And to keep things interesting, we also rolled with the punches - moving away from the TripAdvisor API with not much time left - because Yelp’s API is much more mature and we think we’ve got a great shot at the prize :)

title: AFAR (Advanced First Aid Response System)
tagline: AFAR is a crowdsourced, geolocation-based, flexible software solution designed to save lives in medical emergencies.
description:
I remember on a warm June afternoon on the streets in New York City my friends and I were heading to a park. As I was about to cross the street, I heard my friends yell for my name. When I turned, I saw a man who stopped breathing with some food lodged down the wrong pipe in his throat. The people there who were currently trying to help him clearly did not know first aid and were about to stick their fingers down his mouth. Thankfully, a man and I ran up to him and were able to save him with proper first aid training.
The thing is, what happens when those who know first aid are missing in an emergencies like this?
In New York City and other densely populated places, it can take over 15 minutes for an ambulance to arrive in time to help one in need. In cases such as when people have cardiac arrest, it's common logic that every minute a victim's heart's not beating, the greater the chances of death. We need a way for people in medical emergencies to get help earlier. That's where AFAR comes in.
How does it work?
When a medical emergency happens with no medical professional or First Aid trained people nearby, the AFAR system will be notified of the emergency and its location via text messaging or a mobile app.
The AFAR system will then send the emergency details to all program volunteers that have previously signed up and proved that they are qualified to perform first aid.
At the same time, AFAR will also automatically call 911 or whatever emergency number corresponds to the country of the distress call, thus sending an ambulance or whatever service you need.
Response to medical emergencies will increase and save lives.
Key Features:
-The service fully works. Anyone can sign up as a volunteer on our website right now and will receive any notifications of emergencies near them.
-You do not need to install the app in order to use the emergency service. Simply text it and follow its instructions.
-With the app, you can report emergencies in literally seconds. The app will automatically determine your location for you.
-You can also very quickly search up instructions for all sorts of emergencies, such as allergies, burns, cuts, and head trauma.
-The server will call the correct emergency number for you if you're in a different country. For example, it'll call 999 if the distress call is in Britain or 911 if the distress call is in USA/Canada.
It'll also even speak in the right language for some countries. (Funny sidenote: We never really fully tested this feature because doing so will bring a ambulance to here).

title: Alertr
tagline: Your first defense against assault, helping you get help when you can't help yourself.
description:
Alertr is the LifeAlert of the 21st century, for anyone and everyone who may find themselves in a compromising situation where help being just an arm's reach and a phone call away isn't good enough. It removes the bells and whistles of contacting help, stripping them down to the
simplest
actions possible:
pressing buttons on a Pebble smart watch
.
Our app has the potential to help any user who would like to wear a GPS-enabled help text or a 911 phone call on their wrist. Our app was specifically designed with students and people our age in mind. There is a staggering number of sexual assaults and rapes that have been inadequately investigated, not only on college campuses, but in an average society. This problem has only escalated and likely will continue to run rampant. Our app aims to counter that proliferation of crime--to heel it before it can even poison another community or take the livelihood, or even life, of another victim.
We aim to be a part of rape and assault prevention
, and here's how Alertr helps:
Speed-dial 911
--a
simple two-button protocol
will dispatch a phone call to the police from your phone. Even if you can't talk, because you're impaired or compromised in any way, they can determine your location and even potentially hear the background of your conversations. Our app takes an extra security measure to prevent misdials, by forcing the user to confirm their selection via a combination of button selections prior to dispatching a call to 911.
Send a GPS-location-included preset message to a contact of your choice
--perhaps your situation doesn't warrant a police presence; yet you still feel unsafe. Alertr has a
similar two-button protocol
that will send a text message to a person of your choice. Users will use our companion Android app to program that person's name and phone number. When the feature is activated, a message is sent--letting your emergency contact of choice know where you are and that you need help.
Future developments include allowing multiple emergency contacts (up to 5), a voice recording feature that can be activated from Pebble, and message customization via the companion app.
Alertr makes best use of why and how smart watches will
streamline
and
simplify
our daily lives. It's
straightforward
and
versatile
, potentially serving the needs of many. Alertr is the first defense against assault.

title: alternis.
tagline: find an alternative for anything
description: Our story starts and ends with there being an alternative for pretty much anything that exists these days. As we tried to come up with an idea we found out that many of the things we came up with already existed, so this led us to a take step back, and look at the competition that exists in the market already. Our app is intended to be used by anyone who wants to see what else is out there. We've built a search engine with the goal of finding an alternative or competing product to something you're used to.

title: Amethyst
tagline: It's a rapid framework to create text based programming workshops.
description: We needed to teach an Intro to HTML & CSS workshop. But there wasn't an easy, quick way to create an online programming workshop. What our framework aims to do is that it lets you create workshops in markdown with extra styling features for errors and tips. It provides a way to give beautiful, consistent text based programming workshops.

title: ARM-band
tagline: Universal musical instrument using an easy to use armband
description:
Our Story
Coming from different parts of Canada and Jamaica, we're a team of three programmers who believe in simplicity, reliability, and convenience. We're also extreme fanatics of music, with skills ranging in iOS development, Android development, back-end and front-end. Our combined collaboration, in terms of skills provides us with the tools to perform and this performance is very well portrayed in our project - fun, addictive, and musically appealing.
Our Project
Our product allows you to turn your basic arm movements into musical notes that can be used for easy song composition. Using the MYO armband, we're able to turn the armband's gestures into musical notes for any instrument using the Android platform. Our first instrument for this hackathon is the theremin. On screen, the user is able to select the instrument of their choice (theremin), and compose their music. They also have the option of viewing their arm-pitch-frequency-tone representation on a graph on screen to vary and create more professional sounds. At the end of the composition, the user has the option of replaying their newly made music, and then can be stored in a cloud and compared to other users' compositions for analytics, to make future experiences better.
Key Features
Universal musical instrument
Use of MYO armband
Android app music composer
Target Audience
Professional and amateur musicians
Music enthusiasts

title: Attack Parrot
tagline: Pupil Powered Turret
description: We wanted to try using a Pupil tracking headset, and we wanted to make a turret, so we did both. Our goal was to build something that we would like to play with. Using MIT's Pupil headset and open-source software we tagged a room so that we can get distance information about where the person wearing the headset is looking. Using the location data we moved servos through Arduino to move our 3D printed turret. Then the turret could fire a rubberband. We're pretty excited by the turret and are looking forward to taking it home.

title: BackSafe
tagline: Leveraging social media to keep you safe
description:
Why BackSafe?
Like it or not, the world is becoming an increasingly more dangerous place to live in. We're bombarded with stories every day on television, radio, newspapers, and the internet about bone-chilling incidents that happen to everyday people, sometimes in unlikely places. While at the same time people are often spending more time with their phones and less with their family. You can't help but to think: What if I'm next? What it happens to me?
We want to change all that. What if we can choose to work on projects that help save lives, decrease reaction times in emergencies, help get people the care they need and so much more. BackSafe aims to empower everyday people to do the things they love without fear with a simple time-based tracking system. If you aren't home from your outing by a set time that you pick, a personalized security system kicks in, and the people most important to you are notified immediately (within reason) via text and email. It adds security without being constrictive and helps keep people connected.
We utilize everyday technology like Facebook, text messages, and emails to keep other people informed while maintaining your own sense of privacy. This kind of reassurance is invaluable for anyone, and now, available to everyone - regardless of age, race, gender, sexuality, or socioeconomic status. No longer do you need to feel insecure or afraid: rest assured that we have your back.
On a more personal note, I (Tai) dreamed up the idea not only because its economically viable, and has real world impact, but because I believe (free - cheap) applications can help reduce social inequalities and actually make a difference. I came up with the idea during Harvard's WeCode but due weather problems and limited time we were unable to get anything more than a static web page. I personally believe in the future of a product like this and wanted to bring it to Hack The North because it was something I was personally passionate about building. So we scrapped the past, and built something new for the future with an entirely new team, which was an amazing experience. Especially in terms of how the product grew and developed from the new insight.
What we did:
We were perhaps a bit too ambitious. We were hoping to implement a web app that integrated with email and sms along with Facebook for authentication as well as a mobile ios app. We implemented a website, Facebook auth, tried new technology like Parse, Twilio, and Sendgrid successfully but we also had tons of fun trying out all of the great things here at Hack The North.
